name: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
role: Russian novelist, Soviet dissident and critic of communism and of Western materialism
summary: Solzhenitsyn condemned communism as irredeemable and urged the West to resist it rather than coexist. He rejected violence and revolution in favour of refusing to take part in lies, wanted the Soviet empire dissolved and non-Russian republics free to leave, and pressed for local self-government, private farms and small property with limits on monopoly. He distrusted party-list democracy and unlimited progress, preached duty and self-limitation over rights, and held that politics needs a religious, Orthodox moral base. He criticised the West for weak will, legalism and consumerism.

notes: He held no office after leaving the USSR, so every answer rests on his words: the Nobel lecture, Live Not by Lies, excerpts of the Letter to the Soviet Leaders, the Warning to the West speeches, The Mortal Danger, the Harvard and Templeton addresses, Rebuilding Russia in full and the 2007 Spiegel interview. Searched themes: communism and detente, nations and secession, democracy, elections and parties, local government, land and property, markets and monopoly, family and schools, religion and the state, growth and progress, violence and revolution, the press and culture. Health care, welfare, taxes beyond progressive taxation, drugs, guns, abortion, sex and gender, immigration, the death penalty, technology policy and most economic details had no stated position in the sources found.
